# Bascik

> Bascik is a build tool for HTML components. It scopes and assembles reusable HTML component files into plain HTML pages at build time. It adds zero JavaScript to the output. You write HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; Bascik scopes and assembles them.

Bascik resolves custom HTML tags to component source HTML, scopes CSS and JavaScript, rewrites DOM selectors, and outputs plain static HTML pages with zero framework runtime.

For the complete, centralized developer reference and AI assistant instructions, see [SKILL.md](https://bascik.dev/assets/SKILL.md).

## Philosophy

- [Why Bascik](https://bascik.dev/why-bascik): The guiding principle behind Bascik is simple: use what already exists.
- [Lighthouse 100s](https://bascik.dev/performance): Bascik gives you an enormous head start on Lighthouse scores.
- [Bascik vs Frameworks](https://bascik.dev/vs-frameworks): Bascik is not a framework.

## Start Here

- [Getting Started](https://bascik.dev/getting-started): Bascik requires Node.js v22.18+.
- [CLI / Command Line](https://bascik.dev/cli): Bascik features a simple, fast, and highly informative CLI for both development and production building.
- [Configuration](https://bascik.dev/configuration): Create a bascik.config.ts file in your project root to override any default settings.

## Features

- [Components](https://bascik.dev/components): Components are the core building block in Bascik.
- [Scoped Styles](https://bascik.dev/scoped-styles): Scoped styles namespace a component's CSS at build time, keeping its selectors and animations from leaking into the rest of the page.
- [Scoped JavaScript](https://bascik.dev/scoped-javascript): Write <script> tags directly in your component HTML.
- [Slots](https://bascik.dev/slots): Slots let you pass inner HTML content into a component at the usage site.
- [Props](https://bascik.dev/props): Props let you pass text values into a component template at usage time using data-bascik-prop-* attributes.
- [Attribute Inheritance](https://bascik.dev/attribute-inheritance): Any attribute on a component usage tag that is not a Bascik-specific attribute (data-bascik-*) is automatically merged onto the component's root element.
- [Build Scripts](https://bascik.dev/build-scripts): Build-time scripts let you run Node.js code at transpile time and inject the output directly into the page with no client-side JavaScript required.
- [Production Server](https://bascik.dev/server): Bascik generates static output, HTML, CSS, and JS that a CDN or any file server can deliver.
- [Sitemap & robots.txt](https://bascik.dev/sitemap): Bascik generates a sitemap.xml and robots.txt automatically at build time.
- [JavaScript Libraries](https://bascik.dev/libraries): Bascik does not add any JavaScript to your pages.

## Reference

- [FAQ](https://bascik.dev/faq): Answers to common questions about Bascik.
- [Scoping Compatibility](https://bascik.dev/compatibility): Legend
- [Agent Skill](https://bascik.dev/agent-skill): Download the Bascik skill file and attach it to GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude, or any AI assistant that supports instruction files, so it understands Bascik's component model, ...
- [VS Code Extension](https://bascik.dev/resources/vscode-extension): The Bascik VS Code extension is a lightweight editor companion for the scoping system.
- [Deploying](https://bascik.dev/resources/deploying): Bascik's build output is a standard folder of static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.

## Recipes

- [Markdown](https://bascik.dev/recipes/markdown): Bascik does not ship a Markdown pipeline, but build-time scripts are Node.js, so any Markdown library works.
- [Page-Aware Scripts](https://bascik.dev/recipes/page-aware-scripts): Some pages need content that is specific to the current page, such as a canonical URL in the head, an Open Graph image, a structured-data block, or even a page-specific sidebar.
- [Server Scripts](https://bascik.dev/recipes/server-scripts): data-bascik-server scripts are plain Node.js ESM modules.
- [Templating](https://bascik.dev/recipes/templating): Bascik does not ship a template language or a custom server-side object model.
- [Testing Site Logic](https://bascik.dev/recipes/testing): Bascik projects can include two kinds of scripts: server scripts that run in Node.js on every request, and browser scripts inside components.

## Internals

- [Internals Overview](https://bascik.dev/internals): Everything you need to work on the Bascik package itself, architecture, the transpilation pipeline, the scoping system, the dev server, and how to run the test suite.
- [Architecture](https://bascik.dev/internals/architecture): Bascik is a Node.js CLI tool written in TypeScript.
- [Transpilation Pipeline](https://bascik.dev/internals/transpilation-pipeline): Bascik transforms source HTML into deployable HTML by replacing every custom component tag with its resolved, scoped content.
- [Scoping System](https://bascik.dev/internals/scoping-system): Scoping prevents one component's styles and identifiers from leaking into another.
- [Dev Server](https://bascik.dev/internals/dev-server): Bascik's development server serves transpiled pages from an in-memory store, static assets from disk, and broadcasts live-reload events via Server-Sent Events.
- [Testing Internals](https://bascik.dev/internals/testing): Bascik has two separate test suites: unit tests (Vitest) that verify individual library modules, and end-to-end tests (Playwright) that build and browser-test the full transpila...
- [Create App](https://bascik.dev/internals/create-app): The create/ folder is a small standalone package that scaffolds a fresh Bascik project.
- [CI / CD](https://bascik.dev/internals/ci-cd): Bascik uses two GitHub Actions workflows: one for continuous integration on every push and pull request, and one for publishing releases to npm when a version tag is pushed.

## Switch to Bascik

- [Overview](https://bascik.dev/switch): Moving an existing site to Bascik is mostly a mechanical transformation: extract repeated markup into component files, replace runtime framework logic with build-time equivalent...
- [From Astro](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-astro): Astro and Bascik are both build-time component systems that output zero-JS HTML by default.
- [From Eleventy](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-eleventy): Eleventy is a static site generator; Bascik is a build tool for HTML components.
- [From Hugo](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-hugo): Hugo is a static site generator; Bascik is a build tool for HTML components.
- [From Next.js](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-next): Next.js and Bascik share file-based routing, but Next.js is a full-stack React framework while Bascik is a build-time HTML assembler.
- [From React](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-react): React and Bascik both build UIs from reusable components.
- [From Svelte](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-svelte): Svelte and Bascik share a surface-level resemblance: both use single-file components that combine markup, logic, and scoped styles in one place.
- [From Vue](https://bascik.dev/switch/from-vue): Vue and Bascik are both component-based.
